### Project Name

Maskura

### Project Description

Maskura is the open-source policy boundary between AI agents and object storage: S3-compatible clients (AWS CLI/SDKs, MCP servers, agents) get one place to decide which representation of data crosses that boundary - plaintext, PII-filtered, or envelope-encrypted - bound to the exact policy code that ran. Capabilities: PII redaction; per-field hybrid envelope encryption (X25519 + ML-KEM-768/AES-256-GCM; legacy RSA-OAEP reads); Wasm transform sandbox; signed pipelines (Ed25519/CBOR); passkey (WebAuthn) policy approvals + verifiable evidence bundles; S3 multipart/streaming semantics. Origin: Amit Mor / 231self - the security boundary for agentic AI on regulated S3 data. Open since 2026, Apache-2.0 (v0.7.x).

### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

AAIF operationalizes agentic AI for enterprise scale; enterprises cannot deploy agents over customer data without an auditable answer to 'which data did the agent see, and under whose policy?' Maskura is that infrastructure: agent identity scoping (per-key workspace scope), delegated trust (policy approvals bound to executed code), and security/privacy enforcement (PII filtering + post-quantum-capable encryption) where agents touch object storage. Directly aligned with the Identity & Trust, Security & Privacy, and Governance/Risk WGs.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

No dependencies on existing AAIF projects. Complementary to the Identity & Trust WG's delegation/identity work (scoped credentials and policy-bound data access over S3 APIs) and the Security & Privacy WG's practices (fail-closed policy gates, sandboxed transforms, evidence bundles). We would contribute practical experience enforcing auditable policy over real storage protocols and align credential/delegation formats with WG outputs.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Intended users: teams deploying AI agents and MCP servers over S3-compatible storage with regulated data, and ML pipelines with object-store data.
Use cases: agents receive PII-filtered representations; policy changes require passkey approval and produce verifiable evidence; customer-held private keys decrypt protected fields.
Adoption: early-stage. Public Apache-2.0 releases provide multi-arch images, an SBOM, and S3 conformance tests. No external deployment or design-partner evidence is provided in this proposal. The Sandbox case rests on the project's documented technical thesis.

### Governance Model

Single-maintainer governance: Amit Mor (231self) is maintainer and final decision-maker; decisions recorded as ADRs (docs/adr/), plans in docs/plans/, ownership in OWNERS.md, conventions in AGENTS.md/README. On admission: adopt LF Minimum Viable Governance and expand maintainership.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

GitHub Actions on every PR: format, lint (warnings denied), full test suites (Rust incl. Postgres-backed policy/engine tests, Python, web/Playwright), security jobs (CodeQL, cargo-audit, cargo-deny, dependency review), SDK generation (OpenAPI -> Python/TypeScript), S3 conformance e2e. Releases: semver tags (v0.7.x, ~monthly) via a reusable workflow producing multi-arch images (amd64/arm64), native binaries, Wasm plugins, SDKs, SBOM, SHA256SUMS/IMAGE_DIGESTS, release-smoke gate on the published image.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Public GitHub issues and PRs against the main repository; CONTRIBUTING.md documents the fork and PR process, required tests, and review conventions. Specification changes are recorded as ADRs in docs/adr and reviewed through public PRs. Security reports follow SECURITY.md.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/231self/maskura/issues

### External Project Dependencies

Core Rust dependencies include tokio, axum, hyper, rustls, sea-orm/sqlx, serde (MIT or Apache-2.0), and wasmtime (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions). Node/npm tooling supports the dashboard and SDK tests. The local cargo-deny check passes advisories, bans, licenses, and sources; duplicate-version warnings remain in the dependency graph.

### Maintainers & Contributors

Amit Mor (@amit231self, 231self) is the maintainer. Contribution activity: https://github.com/231self/maskura/commits?author=amit231self

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

Amit Mor (maintainer). Technical decisions are proposed and recorded as ADRs in docs/adr/, roadmap/trade-offs in docs/plans/; the maintainer owns the final call. On admission: LF Minimum Viable Governance with a maintainer council.

### Lifecycle Stage Evidence

Sandbox thesis: (1) Intended users - platform/security teams running AI agents and MCP servers over S3-compatible storage with regulated data. (2) Growth graduation would need a stable 1.0 storage/policy API, adoption beyond the maintainer's organization, another organization contributing regularly, and completed LF governance transition. (3) Why it matters before broad adoption - agent access to regulated object data is the enterprise blocker for agentic AI; the policy-boundary pattern (decisions bound to executed policy code, customer-held keys, verifiable approvals) is rebuilt ad hoc at each organization and deserves a shared auditable reference. Evidence: docs/adr (incl. policy approval and execution trust boundary), docs/encryption.md, docs/security.md, release/e2e suites.

### Security

No OpenSSF Best Practices badge yet. Security reports: security@231self.com or private GitHub reporting (SECURITY.md). CI runs cargo-audit, cargo-deny, dependency review, and CodeQL. The Wasm runtime has memory, table, stack, and fuel limits. Crypto designs and the threat model are documented in docs/encryption.md, docs/security.md, and ADRs. Releases include an SBOM and GitHub provenance attestations.

### Infrastructure Needs or Requests

None beyond standard foundation CI/registry hosting. Current infrastructure: GitHub Actions CI, GitHub Container Registry images, and GitHub Pages for the docs.

### Additional Information

Maskura's distinguishing property is verifiable enforcement: data-plane decisions (which representation crosses the boundary) are bound to the exact policy code that executed, and approvals are customer-verifiable offline (evidence bundles with checkpoint continuity). We will bring this enforcement experience to AAIF working groups on identity, trust, and security/privacy and align with their outputs.
